qt: to the Commission Manolis Kefalogiannis (PPE) Subject:

In a statement issued from the Libyan capital, Tripoli, Türkiye’s energy minister said that, in the context of the illegal memorandum of understanding between Türkiye and Libya, Türkiye stands ready to commence operations within Libya’s maritime zone, sending a reminder of Türkiye’s ‘rights’ in the Eastern Mediterranean. In an amendment to the Recommendation on the situation in Libya approved on 23 November 2022, the European Parliament formally decided that the memorandum of understanding on the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions in the Mediterranean Sea, signed between Libya and Türkiye, does not comply with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and therefore cannot produce any legal consequences for third states. It also calls on the Libyan authorities to proceed with the cancellation of the 2019 memorandum of understanding between Türkiye and Libya, urging them not to implement any clause included in the subsequent agreement on hydrocarbons signed on 3 October 2022, which provides for illegal drilling activities in third countries’ exclusive economic zones, including those of Cyprus and Greece. In view of this: 1.
Is the Commission aware of these statements?
What action and what steps will it take in order to prevent the illegal drilling activities in the EEZ of Greece and Cyprus from going ahead?
at: (English version) to the Commission Manolis Kefalogiannis (PPE) (22 January 2024) Subject: Türkiye’s illegal drilling in the EEZ of Greece and Cyprus In a statement issued from the Libyan capital, Tripoli, Türkiye’s energy minister said that, in the context of the illegal memorandum of understanding between Türkiye and Libya, Türkiye stands ready to commence operations within Libya’s maritime zone, sending a reminder of Türkiye’s ‘rights’ in the Eastern Mediterranean. (17 June 2024) On 3 October 2022, through a statement by the spokesperson (1), the European External Action Service reiterated the known EU position regarding the Türkiye-Libya memorandum of understanding on the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions in the Mediterranean Sea (2). This position was clearly stated in the European Council Conclusions of December 2019 (3). In these conclusions, the European Council emphasised that the above-mentioned Türkiye-Libya memorandum of understanding infringes upon the sovereign rights of third states, does not comply with the Law of the Sea and cannot produce any legal consequences for third states. At the same time, the European Council unequivocally reaffirmed its solidarity with Greece and Cyprus regarding these actions by Türkiye. The position of the EU regarding this matter remains unchanged. The Commission will continue to closely monitor the situation with the highest level of scrutiny and address these concerns in bilateral contacts. The EU Maritime Security Strategy (4) addresses maritime security threats including unauthorised exploration and drilling activities for hydrocarbons in the exclusive economic zones of Member States. In the face of evolving maritime security threats, the Council of the EU in its conclusions of October 2023 (5) reaffirmed EU’s fundamental interests in maritime security and in particular to safeguard Member States’ maritime zones from illegal, unauthorised exploration and drilling activities for hydrocarbons and other resources, in accordance with international law, in particular the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (6).

The EU can impose targeted restrictive measures on persons or entities responsible for, or involved in, unauthorised drilling activities of hydrocarbons in the Eastern Mediterranean. In November 2023, the Council of the EU renewed its restrictive measures (7) imposed in 2019 in view of Türkiye's unauthorised drilling activities in the Eastern Mediterranean, for an additional year, until 30 November 2024. The restrictive measures consist of assets freeze for listed persons and entities, travel ban to the EU, and EU citizens and companies are forbidden from making funds or economic resources available to those listed.
